messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Combining posteriors using model weights
parts:
Hi all.

I am doing some analyses with INLA and would like to pool the posteriors for a
parameter value from two competing models, where the two models have different
model weights (based on information criteria, WAIC). I wrote a function to combine 
the two posteriors, where the weights determine the number of samples from 
each posterior that will be added to the pooled posterior. Does this seem like a
reasonable way to combine posteriors based on model weights? I know there is a 
vast literature on Bayesian Model Averaging that might tell me if my hack is reasonable
or not, but I don't have the chops to find the answer in all that vastness.

I pasted the code below in case (1) it is reasonable approach and (2) it is useful to
someone else. Caution to future readers, read the full thread before using this potentially ridiculous code.

Thanks!
Tim

# simple function to create an aggregate distribution based on weights----------
get_weighted_posterior <- function(dists, wts, summa=T, histo=T){
  # get and test inputs
  nposts <- length(dists)
  if(nposts<2) {
    stop(message="ERROR...there is only one distribution.")}
  nsamps <- length(dists[[1]])
  if(nposts<2 | var(lengths(dists))!=0) {
    stop(message="ERROR...lengths of distributions do not match.")}
  nwts <- length(wts)
  if(nposts!=nwts) {
    stop(message="ERROR...numbers of distributions and weights do not match.")}
  samp_mat <- matrix(unlist(dists), nrow=nsamps, ncol=nposts)
  dist_wts <- unlist(wts)
  if(sum(dist_wts)!=1) {
    stop(message="ERROR...weights do not sum to one.")}
  # make a weighted aggregate distribution
  new_dist <- numeric()
  for(i in 1:nposts){
    subsamp <- sample(samp_mat[,i], size=(nsamps * dist_wts[i]))
    new_dist <- c(new_dist, subsamp)
  }
  # create summaries
  summ <- NULL
  if(summa==T){
  summ <- c(mean=mean(new_dist), sd=sd(new_dist),
            quantile(new_dist, probs=c(0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9,
                                 0.95, 0.975)))
  }
  # plot a histogram
  if(histo==T) hist(new_dist)
  # return list
  return(list(weighted_distribution=new_dist, weights=dist_wts, summaries=summ))
}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# function tests ---------------------------------------------------------------
# two test distributions
n <- 100000
mu1 <- 10; sd1 <- 3
mu2 <- 14; sd2 <- 2
y1 <- rnorm(n, mu1, sd1); hist(y1); summary(y1)
y2 <- rnorm(n, mu2, sd2); hist(y2); summary(y2)

# equal weights
get_weighted_posterior(dists=list(y1, y2), wts=list(0.5, 0.5),
                       summa=T, histo=T)$summaries
c(mean=mean(c(y1,y2)), sd=sd(c(y1,y2)))

# all weight on y1
get_weighted_posterior(dists=list(y1, y2), wts=list(1, 0),
                       summa=T, histo=T)$summaries
c(mean=mean(y1), sd=sd(y1))

# all weight on y2
get_weighted_posterior(dists=list(y1, y2), wts=list(0.00, 1.00),
                                   summa=T, histo=T)$summaries
c(mean=mean(y2), sd=sd(y2))
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# with inla --------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
n <- 100
x <- 1:n
y <- rnorm(n, (2 + 0.5*x - 0.0005*x^2), 5)
df <- data.frame(x=x, x2=x^2, y=y)
plot(y ~ x)

# two models
library(inlabru)
m1 <- bru(y ~ 1 + x, data=df)
m2 <- bru(y ~ 1 + x + x2, data=df)

# model weights
library(dplyr)
waics <- data.frame(model=c("m1", "m2"),
                        waic=c(m1$waic$waic, m2$waic$waic)) %>%
  arrange(waic) %>%
  mutate(delta_waic=waic-min(waic),
         rel_lik=round(exp(-0.5 * delta_waic), 3),
         waic_wts=rel_lik / sum(rel_lik)) %>%
  pull(waic_wts)

# two sets of posteriors
fun1 = function() {return (Intercept + 50 * x)}
s1 <- inla.posterior.sample(50000, m1)
lc1 <- as.numeric(inla.posterior.sample.eval(fun1, s1)); summary(lc1); hist(lc1)

fun2 = function() {return (Intercept + 50 * x + 50 * x2)}
s2 <- inla.posterior.sample(50000, m2)
lc2 <- as.numeric(inla.posterior.sample.eval(fun2, s2)); summary(lc2); hist(lc2)

# weighted posterior
wt_post <- get_weighted_posterior(dists=list(lc1, lc2), wts=list(waics[1], waics[2]),
                       summa=T, histo=T)
wt_post$summaries
